children: Vicor shares rose after the company granted a license to a new original equipment manufacturer with the right to procure Vertical Power Delivery modules covered by Vicor patents from unlicensed suppliers.
The stock rose 10% to $203.05 in after-hours trading Wednesday. Through the close, shares were up 68% this year.
Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) enables high-performance AI compute and network processors fueled at a high current density from a low voltage source.
The licenses can source VPD solutions from unlicensed suppliers. Licensees working with Vicor may earn discounts on licensing royalties for commodity VPD modules from unlicensed suppliers.
Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com
